concepts.name: Angle of Elevation
concepts.description: The angle of elevation is the angle formed between the horizontal line and the line of sight when an observer looks upward at an object. It is commonly used to determine the height of inaccessible objects.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify and measure angles of elevation in practical situations.

concepts.name: Angle of Depression
concepts.description: The angle of depression is the angle formed between the horizontal line and the line of sight when an observer looks downward at an object. It is measured from the horizontal level of the observer.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify angles of depression and distinguish them from angles of elevation.

concepts.name: Line of Sight
concepts.description: The line of sight is the straight line joining the observer's eye to the object being viewed. It forms the hypotenuse of the right triangle used in trigonometric calculations.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to represent the line of sight in diagrams involving heights and distances.

concepts.name: Finding Heights
concepts.description: Trigonometric ratios can be used to determine the height of towers, buildings, trees, and other inaccessible objects by using measured distances and observed angles.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate unknown heights using appropriate trigonometric ratios.

concepts.name: Finding Distances
concepts.description: Known heights and observed angles can be used with trigonometric ratios to determine unknown horizontal distances without direct measurement.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to determine unknown distances using trigonometric relationships.

concepts.name: Real-Life Problem Solving
concepts.description: Applications of trigonometry extend to surveying, navigation, engineering, architecture, aviation, and construction where direct measurements are difficult or impossible.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to solve practical problems involving heights and distances using trigonometric ratios.

concepts.name: Diagram Interpretation
concepts.description: Accurate diagrams help identify known quantities, unknown quantities, and appropriate trigonometric relationships required to solve a problem.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to construct and interpret diagrams for trigonometric applications.

concepts.name: Selection of Appropriate Ratio
concepts.description: Choosing the correct trigonometric ratio depends on the given sides and the unknown quantity in a right-angled triangle.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to select the appropriate trigonometric ratio for solving practical problems.

concepts.name: Multi-Step Applications
concepts.description: Some real-life situations require combining multiple trigonometric calculations to determine final measurements accurately.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to solve multi-step application problems involving heights and distances.

concepts.name: Key Concepts of Applications of Trigonometry
concepts.description: This chapter demonstrates how trigonometric ratios are applied to determine inaccessible heights and distances using angles of elevation and depression.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to apply trigonometric concepts to solve real-world measurement problems involving heights and distances.
